text.title: Reflexion Learning Core Rules
text.summary: Testable rules grounding Reflexion Learning: episode schema and injection, the PDCA phases per SDD task, the four memory files, and pattern confidence calibration. Each pairs a binary check with a sourced rationale; HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override.

section.title: Background
section.p: Rules r-pdca-all-four-phases through r-retry-limit-3 are the four phases of the Reflexion learning loop mapped to SDD task execution. Rules r-four-memory-files through r-archive-stale-patterns give the structure and update rules for the four memory files in .aidocs/memory/. Rule r-confidence-update-formula and the levels below cover confidence scoring levels, update formula, decay rules, and common calibration errors.

list.item: L1 (Spec review): load domain patterns before analysis
L4 (Pre-code): load coding patterns and mistakes for the task domain
L5 (Post-code): run external tests, generate verbal reflection
L6 (Complete): update memory files, close or update session.md
0.9+: High — 5+ uses, validated across contexts, no recent failures
0.3-0.49: Experimental — newly identified, not yet validated

section.reference: Full confidence updater script that patches patterns.md in place

rule.statement: Every episode has attempt_id, timestamp, failure_summary, root_cause, corrective_rule, validated_by.
rule.rationale: Every episode has attempt_id, timestamp, failure_summary, root_cause, corrective_rule, validated_by.

rule.statement: corrective_rule must name a concrete observable (input, threshold, file) — not vague advice.
rule.rationale: corrective_rule must name a concrete observable (input, threshold, file) — not vague advice.

rule.statement: The next attempt MUST receive all open corrective_rules in its system prompt verbatim.
rule.rationale: The next attempt MUST receive all open corrective_rules in its system prompt verbatim.

rule.statement: When a new episode contradicts an older rule, the new rule supersedes — record both ids.
rule.rationale: When a new episode contradicts an older rule, the new rule supersedes — record both ids.

rule.statement: Cap memory at N episodes (default 50); evict by recency × evidence score.
rule.rationale: Cap memory at N episodes (default 50); evict by recency × evidence score.

rule.statement: Every SDD task execution must follow Plan → Do → Check → Act. Skipping any phase degrades the learning signal.
rule.rationale: Reflexion only improves agent quality when all four phases complete. Skipping Check means no reflection is generated; skipping Act means no memory is updated.

rule.statement: Load session.md (if continuing), keyword-filter patterns.md for relevant patterns, keyword-filter mistakes.md for domain warnings. Summarize in 5 bullets before proceeding.
rule.rationale: Loading the entire patterns.md and mistakes.md burns 5-15k tokens of context budget. Keyword filtering to 3-5 relevant entries is both faster and more precise.

rule.statement: Execute the task with loaded patterns applied. Deviate from patterns only with a documented reason. Track which patterns are used.
rule.rationale: Pattern tracking enables usage-count updates in the Act phase, which in turn updates confidence scores.

rule.statement: Evaluate output against each acceptance criterion using external signals (test results, linter, type checker). Report each AC as PASS or FAIL with evidence. Do not self-report PASS without external signal.
rule.rationale: LLMs in self-evaluation exhibit systematic optimism — they report AC as PASS when they would fail against an independent test suite. External tests must be the authoritative signal.

rule.statement: After any PASS: extract a PAT-NNN entry for patterns.md if a novel successful approach was used. After any FAIL: append a MIS-NNN entry to mistakes.md. Update session.md.
rule.rationale: Reflections written immediately after task completion are accurate. Reflections written at session end produce generic patterns ("write tests first") without project-specific context.

rule.statement: Set a maximum of 3 Reflexion retry attempts per task. After 3 cycles, escalate to human review.
rule.rationale: Reflexion improves on first and second retry but has diminishing returns. A third failure with updated reflections indicates a gap that verbal reinforcement cannot fix alone.

rule.statement: Maintain exactly four memory files in `.aidocs/memory/`: patterns.md, mistakes.md, decisions.md, session.md. Keep them in the same repository as the code they govern.
rule.rationale: Memory files in a different repo from the code produce context drift — patterns reference files and patterns that no longer exist in the agent's working tree.

rule.statement: A PAT-NNN entry must include: domain, context (when it applies), problem it solves, solution (actionable steps or code), confidence score, usage count, and source task ID.
rule.rationale: Patterns without context cannot be retrieved accurately. Patterns without confidence scores cannot be prioritized by the agent during Plan phase loading.

rule.statement: Write patterns in "When X, do Y" format, not as descriptions of what worked. "When migrating tables with >100k rows, batch the update" not "batching worked well".
rule.rationale: Prescriptive patterns are directly actionable. Descriptive patterns require the agent to re-derive the action, introducing drift.

rule.statement: Clear session.md at the start of each new project. Session context from a previous project causes the agent to apply irrelevant patterns and miss-attribute mistakes.
rule.rationale: Session.md is project-scoped. Multi-agent pipelines sharing session.md across projects produce write conflicts and corrupted context.

rule.statement: Archive patterns with confidence below 0.3 or unused for 90+ days into patterns-archive.md. Do not delete — archived patterns may be relevant again if the domain returns.
rule.rationale: Stale patterns loaded in context introduce noise. High-scoring but untouched patterns may have been invalidated by framework upgrades or architectural changes.

rule.statement: Apply the confidence update formula after each task outcome: success → min(0.95, score + 0.05); partial → score * 0.95; failure → max(0.30, score - 0.15).
rule.rationale: Symmetric updates would allow a single failure to destroy high-confidence patterns. The asymmetric formula requires consistent failures to reduce confidence significantly.

rule.statement: If preconditions in AGENTS.md "Applies If" do not all hold, OR any "Skip If" disqualifier is true, do not run this methodology — route to the named alternative.
rule.rationale: Methodologies are pre-condition gated; running them out-of-scope produces noise and burns the agent context budget.

rule.statement: If preconditions hold, execute the procedure in `content/04-procedure.xml` (or the rule set above when complexity is light), emit the artefact specified by `content/02-output-contract.xml`, and validate with `scripts/validate-reflexion-learning.py` before returning.
rule.rationale: Tying the entry rule to the validator script closes the loop between policy and machine check.
